title: Sell Mineral Rights in Pollard, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Pollard, AL | Escambia County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Pollard, AL in the Vocation Field area of Escambia County? Get a courthouse-checked offer, no pressure to sign.
heroLead: Pollard sits in Escambia County not far from the Vocation Field, one of the deepest and highest-pressure gas discoveries onshore Alabama, drilled into the Norphlet formation well below the older, shallower production most of south Alabama is known for.
intro: Deep Norphlet gas condensate tests like the ones at Vocation Field represent a different scale of drilling than the shallow oil wells that dot most of south Alabama — deeper, more expensive, and typically undertaken only by operators with the capital to handle the pressures involved. Families near Pollard whose land sits within reach of that deep trend sometimes hold interests that were leased specifically for that kind of exploration, with different terms and different economics than a typical shallow lease.

sections.heading: Deep Norphlet Gas vs. Shallow Production
paragraphs: If your family's Pollard-area lease was tied to deep Norphlet exploration rather than shallower production, the well economics and royalty structure can look quite different from what a neighbor with shallow production might see. We check which type of well or unit your interest is actually connected to before pricing it.

sections.heading: A Rail Town's Older Land Records
paragraphs: Pollard grew up as a rail community, and a lot of the surrounding farmland has stayed in the same families since well before any deep gas exploration reached this part of Escambia County. We trace that older ownership at the Escambia County Courthouse in Brewton before we say anything about a mineral interest's current status.

faqs.question: Is our interest tied to a deep gas well or an older shallow one?
faqs.answer: We check the specific unit and well depth for your tract, since deep Norphlet gas and shallow oil production are priced very differently.

faqs.question: Our lease terms look unusual compared to what we've heard from neighbors. Why?
faqs.answer: Deep, high-pressure gas leases in this area sometimes carry different terms than typical shallow leases. We review your specific lease language before pricing an offer.

faqs.question: How do we confirm our family's original land records near Pollard?
faqs.answer: We pull the Escambia County deed and probate records ourselves once we have the legal description or a family name to search under.

faqs.question: Would you buy an interest that's never actually produced but sits near the deep gas trend?
faqs.answer: Yes, we consider that kind of speculative interest, priced against nearby activity rather than a producing royalty.

faqs.question: Who do we contact first if we've never dealt with a mineral sale before?
faqs.answer: Just send us what you have, even if it's incomplete. We'll walk you through what we find and what the process looks like from there.
